presets.name: Sepia
presets.description: The style keeps a light, a mid and a deep tone and hands them out down the pile. A monochrome set moves all three at once and leaves the arrangement alone.

presets.name: Greyscale
presets.description: The same three step ladder without any hue. Useful for a print stylesheet or anywhere color would carry meaning it should not.

presets.name: Duotone
presets.description: Background and all three stones take the same hue at four lightnesses, which is as close to a single color as a pile of stones can get and still read as stacked.

presets.name: Muted
presets.summary: Dusty stones instead of the shipped eight.
presets.description: The shipped tones are already quiet. These go one step further toward grey, which suits a page where the avatar should not be the loudest thing on it.

presets.name: Electric
presets.summary: Stones past anything the style ships.
presets.description: The same lever the other way. The ground goes near black so the pile reads as lit rather than printed, and the deep tone has to come up with it: the shipped one is dark enough to lose the bottom stone against the ground.

presets.name: Pastel Wall
presets.summary: Colored grounds instead of the paper whites.
presets.description: The style ships four near white backgrounds that barely differ. Five pale colors make the ground a choice rather than a default.

presets.name: Bold Pop
presets.description: Loud enough that the avatar holds its own against a busy page. The light stones are what carry the silhouette against it.

presets.name: Sunrise
presets.summary: A warm gradient behind the pile.
presets.description: Shows the gradient background options: two colors, a linear fill and a fixed angle. The seed still decides which of the two ends up on top.

presets.name: Stencil
presets.summary: One ground for everyone, only the pile varies.
presets.description: Every avatar gets the same near black ground, so nothing distinguishes them but the arrangement. That turns a set from a group of pictures into an icon sheet.

presets.name: Tower
presets.description: Four of the eleven layouts stack four stones or more. Kept on their own, every avatar is a column, and the width of each stone becomes the thing that separates one from the next.

presets.name: Close Up
presets.summary: Scaled in, so the pile fills the frame.
presets.description: Uses scale rather than color. The bottom stone runs past the edge, which reads better at the size a comment thread gives an avatar.
